  "text": "Ada caught the chain before it reached the keyhole. It pulled against her fingers, gently at first, then hard enough to cut her skin.

Upstairs, a door opened.

“There’s no one else in the house,” the constable said.

Venn’s wife looked at the open tin. “There is now.”

A wet footprint appeared on the bottom stair. A second darkened the wood above it. The constable swung his lantern toward the landing, but the light showed only the banister and the closed doors beyond.

Elias gripped Ada’s shoulder. “Put it back.”

Ada tried to lower the chain into the tin. It would not bend. Its links stood straight between her hand and the cellar door, trembling like a wire under tension.

The keyhole clicked.

Venn’s wife seized the empty sleeve from the floor and wrapped it around Ada’s hand. The pull ceased. For an instant the sleeve filled out, its damp fingers closing over hers. Ada cried out and dropped the chain.

It struck the tiles. The footprints on the stairs vanished.

The constable knelt beside the cellar door. “Venn?” he called.

Something answered from directly behind him, in his own voice. “Venn?”

He turned so quickly the lantern hit the wall. Glass broke. In the brief flare before the flame died, Ada saw a figure at the kitchen threshold: a man in a constable’s coat, dripping water onto the tiles.

Then the room went dark. The real constable was still kneeling by the door. Ada could hear him breathing.

From the threshold, his voice said, “Which one of us has the key?”"
